pattern.crimePattern: chase-vehicle driver kills the balloon crew chief who caught him selling the company's propane, and moves her to the landing site
pattern.notes: Fictional balloon company, conservancy and lodge. Balloon operations shown in outline (inflation, chase vehicles, landing breakfast); the cultural reader is asked to check them. No propane handling detail beyond counting cylinders.

ob.text: A balloon safari company reports its ground-crew chief, Naserian Nkoitoi (31), found dead under the folded balloon envelope at the morning landing site on the plains beside Enkare Conservancy at 07:35. Recorded as a suspected landing accident.

people.name: Naserian Nkoitoi
people.bio: The company's first woman crew chief. Counts every propane cylinder after every launch, with a pencil and a tick.

people.name: Musyoki Mutunga
people.bio: Eleven years with the company. Drives the vehicle that tows the fan trailer.

people.name: Graham Fenwick
people.bio: Born in Nanyuki. Thirty years flying balloons over the Mara. Argued with Naserian about the wind.

facts.text: Naserian Nkoitoi, ground-crew chief, was found dead under the folded balloon envelope at the landing site at 07:35. Recorded as a suspected landing accident.
One head wound. Damp mud on her boots and the back of her jacket.
Base radio log, 06:25, Naserian: "Balloon away, launch clear, counting cylinders."
Base radio log, 07:00: base calls Naserian. No answer.
Base radio log, 07:35, Musyoki: "Naserian is under the envelope!"
Guests' photos, 07:22–07:35: the landing and the toast. Naserian is in none of them. Chase vehicle 2 arrives in the background at 07:28.
The landing site is dry red soil and short, grazed grass.
The launch site is damp black cotton clay with long, seeding grass.
Fleet tracker: vehicle 1 left the launch site at 06:20. Vehicle 2 stayed at the launch site from 06:20 to 06:52, then drove to the landing site, arriving 07:28.
Cylinder register: three serial tags missing from today's count. Naserian's ticks stop at cylinder 9 of 12. In the margin: "Zablon — Talek lodge store?"
In the Talek lodge store: three cylinders with their serial tags filed off, the Sunrise logo still faint under new paint.
Zablon's PesaPap receipts: weekly payments to MUSYOKI MUTUNGA since October.
Records, Musyoki's PesaPap: weekly receipts from Z. ONKWARE since October.
Records, Musyoki's line: launch-site zone 06:15–06:50; landing-site zone from 07:25.
Vehicle 2's toolbox: a cylinder valve wrench with a hexagonal jaw, washed. The lid's rubber seal has a smear.
In vehicle 2's fan trailer: a spare envelope cover, folded wet, with black clay and long-grass seeds in its folds.
Payroll: January wages paid in full to every crew member on 31 January.
Crew file: Naserian was the only applicant for crew chief last year. Musyoki didn't apply.
Flight GPS log: airborne from 06:15 to 07:20 with twelve guests.
Flight log, pre-flight: "Wind marginal (crew chief). Go decision: pilot."
Kerubo: Zablon opened the lodge store with her at 06:30, as every day, an hour's drive from the launch site.
Nkirote was at the base radio all morning; her own log entries run every few minutes from 05:30.
Autopsy: a single blow with a heavy metal tool with a hexagonal jaw.
Autopsy: no crush injuries of the kind a landing basket causes, no burns, no trampling.
Autopsy: lividity shows she lay curled on her side for a while, and was then laid flat.
Autopsy: death between 06:25 and 07:00.
Lab: the clay and seeds on her boots and jacket are from the launch site, not the landing site.
Lab: Naserian's blood in the jaw of the valve wrench.
Musyoki: "I left the launch site with Simon at twenty past six and found her at the landing site."
Musyoki admits he stayed at the launch site after vehicle 1 left, "to load the fan".
Musyoki: "She was counting. She was fine when I left."
Simon: "Both vehicles left together at 06:20."
Simon: he went ahead alone with the breakfast at 06:20, against the rule, and set up the table at the landing site.
Graham: "I was flying twelve guests over the Mara."
Graham: "She said the wind was marginal. She was right. I was lucky."
Zablon: "I bought gas from Musyoki. I didn't ask where from."

topics.reply: Tags fall off. The cage is old. Ask the camp to buy a new one.

interrogations.intro: Simon keeps glancing at the fleet office. "Both vehicles left together at 06:20. That's the rule."
Graham is folding the burner covers and doesn't stop. "I fly. The ground is the crew's business."

topics.reply: She said the wind was marginal. She was right. I was lucky. It's in my log; read it.

interrogations.intro: Zablon stands among his flour sacks, not meeting your eye. "I bought gas from Musyoki. I didn't ask where from."

topics.reply: I never met her. I opened the store at half past six this morning. Kerubo opens the kitchen with me every day.

interrogations.intro: Nkirote has the base log open in front of her and her headset round her neck. "She called at twenty-five past six. Then nothing."

contradictions.reaction: "...I stayed to load the fan. She was counting. She was fine when I left."
"I went ahead. We're not supposed to. The breakfast was late. Musyoki stayed behind."
Musyoki looks at the lab sheet for a long time. "Three cylinders," he says. "Three. She would have had me sacked for three cylinders." Then he stops.

timeOfDeath.note: Alive on the radio at 06:25; vehicle 2 left the launch site with her at 06:52. The autopsy allows 06:25–07:00.

proof.concludes: Naserian was alive at the launch site at 06:25 and died soon after. The clay on her boots is the launch site's; she lay curled up before she was laid flat, and she never reached the landing site alive.
Simon left at 06:20; Musyoki and vehicle 2 stayed at the launch site until 06:52. She died between 06:25 and 06:52, and Musyoki "found" her at 07:35.
Musyoki has been selling the company's propane to a Talek lodge store for months; Naserian's count stopped three short.

The valve wrench in his toolbox carries her blood, and the trailer cover holds the launch-site clay. At the launch site, Musyoki Mutunga struck Naserian with a cylinder valve wrench because she'd caught him stealing and selling the company's propane.

eliminations.why: Her boots carry the launch site's clay, she's in none of the landing photos, and she lay curled up somewhere else first.
Vehicle 2 didn't move from the launch site until 06:52, after she was dead.
She radioed from the launch site at 06:25, an hour from Talek, and was dead within half an hour.
She never came back to the camp; the camp was calling her at 07:00.
Graham was in the air with twelve guests from 06:15 to 07:20.
Simon left the launch site at 06:20 and was setting up breakfast. He broke the rule; he didn't kill her.
Zablon was opening the lodge store in Talek, an hour away.
Nkirote was at the base radio all morning, logging every few minutes.
No crush injuries, and she died at the launch site, not the landing.
One blow from a tool with a hexagonal jaw, not a fall.
That argument was the pilot's, and he was flying.
Splitting up was Simon's rule-breaking, not a motive.
Every crew member was paid in full on 31 January.
Musyoki never applied for the crew-chief post.

reconstruction.text: For months Musyoki takes two or three full propane cylinders a week from the cage and sells them to the Talek lodge store. Zablon pays by PesaPap and doesn't ask.
Thursday, 06:15. The balloon lifts with Graham and twelve guests. At 06:20 Simon drives ahead with the breakfast, against the rule. Musyoki stays behind "to load the fan".
06:25. Naserian radios: "Balloon away, launch clear, counting cylinders." At cylinder 9 she stops ticking. Three tags are missing.
About 06:30 she confronts him. He strikes her once with the valve wrench, wraps her in the spare envelope cover and lays her in the fan trailer.
06:52, vehicle 2 leaves the launch site. While the guests toast the landing, he lays her under the folded envelope. At 07:35 he shouts on the radio that he's found her.
